Please advise to Customer that or update from your side that Work profile filled in incorrectly in the wrong filed 

It should be in VAT field.

!image-20240119-084703.png|width=584,height=636!

Please be aware that we should not reissue any invoice upon request for the reasons like: no NIP number at the time of issuance and rider provide the number later, rider requests change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoice for these reasons.

Unless it is our mistake, e.g. the value, subject of the sale, or NIP number is wrongly stated by us, then we reissue the invoice. And we need to report VAT for the new invoice.



So if the rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own sake in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

h3. {color:#00b8d9}Reviewed the data and tickets for each issue tag {color}[{color:#00b8d9}here{color}|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1r-0SjTZ8k4LaVe8KE5uWUbmXCYLYOql9h4NgH5D2LSg/edit#gid=205753551]{color:#00b8d9}. Main observations:{color}

* Agents mix up the 4 issue tags as all of them sound similar, and sometimes riders might give information that is applicable to all of them. It is important to clearly define differences between 4 of them.
* *My driver refused to pick me up* - D arrived and *there is a reason* why he refused to complete the ride.
* *My driver refused to wait for me* - D arrived and *didn't wait long enough*. The main problem must be the waiting.
* *My driver didn't show up* - if the main issue is the cancellation fee - follow the cancellation fee process. If the cancellation fee wasn't charged, or R is not complaining about that - follow this process.
* *My driver asked to cancel the ride* - check R & D communication in Admin. If D asked to cancel - follow the process, if didn't - follow the cancellation fee process. 
** This issue might be related to an offline trip. Should be escalated to Safety then.
* Suggestion for Training - teach agents to encourage R & D communication in-app. Some cases could be resolved between R & D, without CS.

Analyzed the code based on tidbits from that thread. So far a potential approach looks like this:

* there is a RiderX-owned internal endpoint {{/internal/getActiveOrderProperties}}
* Campaigns call this to get the AO properties, AO rules can be set up through Admin
* AO rules support {{number}}, {{string}}, and {{boolean}} types; basic checks can be done on those

The response from {{/internal/getActiveOrderProperties}} is a Map with {{string}} keys. It can be freely extended from RiderX side, zero code changes required in Campaign - as long as we stick to the basic types and basic checks.

For example, a new Boolean property {{DROPOFF_IS_AIRPORT}} can be added. {{/internal/getActiveOrderProperties}} can call a Geo endpoint to determine the value for this flag. There’s also a cache for these properties on RiderX side, so this Geo call would happen only once per AO (unless Redis dies, which should be a rare event).

The downside is that this approach could not be set up for individual airports. It can be controlled on per-city level through Targeting though.

Query by Sabrina
(or check Looker [here|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/sql/mvs8sstzh9hdgb], but change the dates)
(Databricks seems not available, because there’s no ST_Intersects function)

**

{noformat}WITH
new_user_cohort AS (
	SELECT
	  DATE(install_time) as date_day
	  , country
	  , city
	  , zone_name
	  , COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN diff_day <= 14 THEN user_id ELSE NULL END) as fod_cohort_14days
	  , COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN diff_day <= 28 THEN user_id ELSE NULL END) as fod_cohort_28days
	  , COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN trait_id = 145 AND diff_day <= 14 THEN user_id ELSE NULL END) as fom_cohort_14days
	  , COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN trait_id = 145 AND diff_day <= 28 THEN user_id ELSE NULL END) as fom_cohort_28days
	FROM( 
    SELECT 
	    af.install_time
	    , af.event_date
	    , DATE_DIFF('day', DATE(af.install_time), af.event_date) AS diff_day
	    , ffr.master_user_id AS user_id
	    , ffr.city 
	    , ffr.country  
	    , pt.trait_id
		, cz.name AS zone_name
    FROM ng_public.etl_first_finished_order_for_user AS ffr
    LEFT JOIN ng_public.etl_appsflyer_first_order_delivered AS af ON ffr.master_user_id  = af.user_id
    LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.delivery_order_order AS oo ON oo.id = ffr.order_id
  	LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.delivery_provider_provider_trait AS pt ON oo.provider_id = pt.provider_id AND pt.trait_id = 145
		LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.etl_delivery_city_zones AS cz 
			ON oo.city_id = cz.city_id 
			AND ST_Intersects(ST_GeometryFromText(cz.geometry_loc), ST_Point(CAST(oo.delivery_lng AS double), CAST(oo.delivery_lat AS double)))
    WHERE af.install_time BETWEEN date'2024-01-01' AND date'2024-01-07' 
    	AND ffr.city = 'Tallinn'
    GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
    )
  WHERE country IS NOT NULL AND city IS NOT NULL
	GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
    
 , total_sign_up AS (
	SELECT
		du.created_date
		, cz.name AS zone_name
		, c.city_name
		, c.country_name
		, COUNT(du.user_id) AS total_sign_up
	FROM ng_delivery.delivery_user_delivery_user AS du
	LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.etl_delivery_city_zones AS cz 
		ON du.city_id = cz.city_id 
		AND ST_Intersects(ST_GeometryFromText(cz.geometry_loc), ST_Point(CAST(du.lng AS double), CAST(du.lat AS double)))
	LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.etl_cities AS c ON c.city_id = du.city_id
	WHERE du.created_date BETWEEN date'2024-01-01' AND date'2024-01-07' 
		AND du.city_id = 1
	GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
    
 , total_order AS (
	SELECT
		oo.created_date
		, c.city_name
		, c.country_name
		, cz.name AS zone_name
		, COUNT(oo.id) AS total_order
		, COUNT(CASE WHEN pt.trait_id = 145 THEN oo.id END) total_market_order
		, COUNT(CASE WHEN oo.created = upu.delivery_app_first_purchase THEN oo.id END) AS total_first_delivery_order
		, COUNT(CASE WHEN oo.created = upu.first_market_vertical_purchase THEN oo.id END) AS total_first_market_order
	FROM ng_delivery.delivery_order_order AS oo
	LEFT JOIN ng_public.etl_user_products_usage AS upu ON oo.master_user_id = upu.user_id AND oo.created = upu.delivery_app_first_purchase
  LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.delivery_provider_provider_trait AS pt ON oo.provider_id = pt.provider_id AND pt.trait_id = 145
	LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.etl_cities AS c ON c.city_id = oo.city_id 
	LEFT JOIN ng_delivery.etl_delivery_city_zones AS cz 
		ON oo.city_id = cz.city_id 
		AND ST_Intersects(ST_GeometryFromText(cz.geometry_loc), ST_Point(CAST(oo.delivery_lng AS double), CAST(oo.delivery_lat AS double)))
	WHERE oo.state = 'delivered'
		AND oo.created_date BETWEEN date'2024-01-01' AND date'2024-01-07'
		AND oo.city_id = 1
	GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)

, final_table AS(
	SELECT 
		date_day
		, country
		, city
		, zone_name
		, fod_cohort_14days
		, fod_cohort_28days
		, fom_cohort_14days
		, fom_cohort_28days
		, 0 AS total_sign_up
		, 0 AS total_order
		, 0 AS total_market_order
		, 0 AS total_first_delivery_order
		, 0 AS total_first_market_order
	FROM new_user_cohort
	
	UNION ALL
	SELECT 
		created_date
		, country_name
		, city_name
		, zone_name
		, 0 AS fod_cohort_14days
		, 0 AS fod_cohort_28days
		, 0 AS fom_cohort_14days
		, 0 AS fom_cohort_28days
		, total_sign_up
		, 0 AS total_order
		, 0 AS total_market_order
		, 0 AS total_first_delivery_order
		, 0 AS total_first_market_order
	FROM total_sign_up
	
	UNION ALL
	SELECT 
		created_date
		, country_name
		, city_name
		, zone_name
		, 0 AS fod_cohort_14days
		, 0 AS fod_cohort_28days
		, 0 AS fom_cohort_14days
		, 0 AS fom_cohort_28days
		, 0 AS total_sign_up
		, total_order
		, total_market_order
		, total_first_delivery_order
		, total_first_market_order
	FROM total_order
)

SELECT
	date_day
	, country
	, city
	, zone_name
	, SUM(fod_cohort_14days) AS fod_cohort_14days
	, SUM(fod_cohort_28days) AS fod_cohort_28days
	, SUM(fom_cohort_14days) AS fom_cohort_14days
	, SUM(fom_cohort_28days) AS fom_cohort_28days
	, SUM(total_sign_up) AS total_sign_up
	, SUM(total_order) AS total_delivery_order
	, SUM(total_market_order) AS total_market_order
	, SUM(total_first_delivery_order) AS total_first_delivery_order
	, SUM(total_first_market_order) AS total_first_market_order
FROM final_table
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4{noformat}

1) For energy drinks, we should implement a buyer verification process similar to that used for alcohol. When a buyer places an order for an energy drink, they must confirm that they are at least 18 years old. It is the courier's responsibility to check the buyer's ID if there are any suspicions that the buyer might be below 18. The courier should then make a note in the app indicating that the age verification has been completed.

{quote}[Article 6 1 . of the Law on Food|https://e-seimas.lrs.lt/portal/legalAct/lt/TAD/74505e2018da11e6aa14e8b63147ee94?jfwid=rivwzvpvg]
_It shall be prohibited to sell, purchase or otherwise transfer energy drinks to persons under the age of 18._ *_The salespersons_* _of energy drinks shall_ *_have the right to and, when doubts arise t_*_hat a person is younger than the age of 18,_ *_must require from the person purchasing energy drinks to present a document_* _proving his identity. Should such a person_ *_fail to produce a document_* _proving his identity, the salespersons of energy drinks_ *_must refuse to sell_* _him the energy drinks._{quote}

The courier must be aware of the age thresholds—20 years for alcohol and 18 years for energy drinks. This information can be conveyed by either including the age requirement in the drink description or implementing a notification system for couriers based on the product ordered. In there is no such a feature, couriers must be explicitly informed about the age restrictions.

2) A license is not required for the sale of energy drinks. There are no sales hours restrictions when energy drinks can be sold.

Some ideas I had when looking at this:

1) we need a new page, i.e. “TopUpProcessing” with url “/topup/processing”. In addition to that we probably should create new backend  API endpoint to return some enum to affect flow instead of attempting to parse the URL returned - i.e. TopUpWebFlow.NATIVE vs TopUpWebFlow.DEFAULT. 

2) We redirect to this new page if our createTopUp backend call tells us this is a different kind of challenge. This has some loading GIF and maybe a button to manually close it? In essence, this page replaces the page made by Payments team with a single button to start for example GooglePay flow - we do that call immediately.

3) When we enter this page, we make some async/AJAX call to actually trigger the native link - I’m not sure if when we do a call via {{window.location.href}}, does this still keep our old page up in the background, but I think this is not important. 

_For reference: these native calls are currently done on the_ [_payment.bolt.eu_|http://payments.bolt.eu] _page that our backend tells the balance webapp to navigate to (TopUpResponse url param)._ 

4) iOS native “app” draws itself on top of the app UI, but something is still visible from the app page in the background. Same is true for the Android native UI. 

5) User completes this challenge one way or another (success or error). In terms of the challenge itself, the question is if we know if the challenge was successfully completed or not. If we do know, we can already go to the success or error page, and like now, tell the user that “we are processing all of this in the background”. Theres even a notification in Bolt app later on if your balance topup went through it seems.

6) To make all of this cooler or if we don’t have a way of knowing if the “challenge” part itself was successful or not, we could look at the question whether the topup/payment in the backend was successful or not. 

For this we could poll the backend for example every 1s (or 2-3s) for a total maximum of 60s (or some other timeout). 

Perhaps if we have some websocket logic possible, we could use that instead of spamming requests. 

Another alternative to websocket is to actually do a longpolling call - open a long request, perhaps max 55s. This listens to an event or keeps regularly checking some other endpoint/query and only returns a response once the event is received or the max time has been reached (lets us either listen to our event or do the “DDOSing” internally). Not sure however if this pattern/architecture is recommended or not.

import re

def batch(iterable, n=1):
    l = len(iterable)
    for ndx in range(0, l, n):
        yield iterable[ndx:min(ndx + n, l)]



input_file_name = 'delivery_fee_set_to_0.csv'
output_file_name = 'updateStatements_delivery_fee_0.txt'
with open(output_file_name, 'w') as output_file:
    line_count = 0
    with open(input_file_name) as input_file:
        csv_reader = csv.reader(input_file, delimiter=',')
        my_list = list(csv_reader)
    my_list = my_list[1:]


    for x in batch(my_list, 1000):
        master_baskets_ids = list(map(lambda y: y[0], x))
        user_basket_ids = list(map(lambda y: y[1], x))
        update_query = f"""
UPDATE taxify_delivery_basket.master_basket SET delivery_price = 0 WHERE id IN ({', '.join(master_baskets_ids)});
            """
        output_file.write(update_query.replace("\n", " ") + "\n")

        update_query = f"""
UPDATE taxify_delivery_basket.user_basket SET delivery_price = 0 WHERE id IN ({', '.join(user_basket_ids)});
            """
        output_file.write(update_query.replace("\n", " ") + "\n")

def batch(iterable, n=1):
    l = len(iterable)
    for ndx in range(0, l, n):
        yield iterable[ndx:min(ndx + n, l)]



input_file_name = 'delivery_fee_set_to_0.csv'

with open(output_file_name, 'w') as output_file:

        csv_reader = csv.reader(input_file, delimiter=',')

        master_baskets_ids = list(map(lambda y: y[0], x))
        user_basket_ids = list(map(lambda y: y[1], x))

        update_query = f"""

The meaning behind the word “contract” is explained more throughly in the same Terms and Conditions section 4.

In another words, confirming a journey with a driver leads to a separate agreement between the passenger and the driver. This means that the driver is acting as a service provider to whom the customer has accepted to pay for the received service. Communication of the terms of the contract are done through the Bolt online platform, including details like the pickup location, destination, fare, and any additional conditions. Other legal responsibilities are brought out in the Terms and Conditions.

It's important to clarify that Bolt is a facilitator in connecting customers with drivers, but the direct contractual relationship is between the customer and the driver. Bolt acts as an intermediary and has its terms of service that users agree to, but it is not a party to the specific transportation contract.

{code:sql}WITH u AS (SELECT unit
           FROM unnest(sequence(0, 59))
                    AS s(unit)),

     t AS (SELECT concat(cast(h.unit AS varchar), ':', -- hours
                         cast(m.unit AS varchar), ':', -- minutes
                         cast(s.unit AS varchar)) AS t -- seconds
           FROM u h
                    CROSS JOIN u m, u s
           WHERE h.unit < 24), -- there are only 24 (0-23) hours in a day

     d AS (SELECT cast("date" AS varchar) AS d
           FROM ng_public.dim_calendar
           WHERE "date" >= date '2024-01-08'
             AND "date" < date '2024-01-15'),

     td AS (SELECT cast(concat(d.d, ' ', t.t) AS timestamp) AS "timestamp"
            FROM d
                     CROSS JOIN t),

     v AS (SELECT v.id                                             AS vehicle_id,
                  concat(m.manufacturer_name, ' ', m.display_name) AS model
           FROM ng_carsharing.rental_car_vehicle_fleet_vehicle v
                    JOIN ng_carsharing.rental_car_config_vehicle_model m
                         ON v.model_id = m.id
           WHERE lower(m.manufacturer_name) NOT LIKE 'bolt%'),

     tdv AS (SELECT *
             FROM td
                      CROSS JOIN v),

     e AS (SELECT *
           FROM (SELECT created_date,
                        vehicle_id,
                        search_category_id,
                        value_new AS state,
                        created   AS started_at
                 FROM ng_carsharing.rental_car_vehicle_vehicle_state_event
                 WHERE type = 'state')),

     tdve AS (SELECT tdv."timestamp",
                     tdv.vehicle_id,
                     e.search_category_id,
                     e.state,
                     sum(if(e.state IS NOT NULL, 1, 0))
                         OVER (PARTITION BY tdv.vehicle_id ORDER BY tdv."timestamp") AS grp
              FROM tdv
                       LEFT JOIN e
                                 ON tdv."timestamp" = e.started_at
                                     AND tdv.vehicle_id = e.vehicle_id),

     tdve_2 AS (SELECT "timestamp",
                       vehicle_id,
                       coalesce(search_category_id,
                                first_value(search_category_id)
                                OVER(PARTITION BY vehicle_id, grp ORDER BY "timestamp")) AS search_category_id,
                       coalesce(state,
                                first_value(state)
                                OVER(PARTITION BY vehicle_id, grp ORDER BY "timestamp")) AS state
                FROM tdve),

     cc AS (SELECT ca.id,
                   ci.name AS city,
                   co.name AS country
            FROM ng_carsharing.rental_car_config_search_category ca
                     JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city ci
                          ON ca.city_id = ci.id
                     JOIN ng_public.admin_system_country co
                          ON ci.country_code = co.code)

SELECT date_format("timestamp", '%Y-%m-%d') AS dt,
       vehicle_id,
       cc.country,
       cc.city,
       tdve_2.state,
       count(*)                             AS total_time_spent_sec
FROM tdve_2
         JOIN cc
              ON tdve_2.search_category_id = cc.id
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
HAVING tdve_2.state IS NOT NULL
   AND tdve_2.state != 'deactivated'{code}

*How to measure effect of Courier ETA on accuracy of Total ETA?*

Main usage is flow is following. 
Customer opens an app => Courier ETAs from all providers to user address are calculated => Courier ETAs are used as a feature to Total ETA model which estimates full time until order is delivered (together with preparation and all other steps)

*_Component importance:_*

Courier ETAs is second most important feature (after predicted preparation time) of total time model. It is responsible for ~20-33% of final accuracy

*_How is it implemented now for Search step:_*

On the model training step the historic haversine distance from provider to client is calculated. Distance is multiplied by historic config speed. Resulting value is used to populate {{courier_from_provider_to_client_duration}} on Search model.
=> Change of value logic on production would actually break the model now

*_What is currently in development from DS:_*

Since summer the {{courier_from_provider_to_client_duration}} that was used on production is saved to {{delivery_eta_eta}} table also for a Search step. Which means that DS could use this value directly instead of reverse engineering it. After this change is implemented the work on this epic could start.

*DSAR Request:* “Hello, please provide me with data of the last trip including the information when the car was locked and unlocked during yesterday’s trip. Thank you.”

A. *Recommendation:*
The request shows that the Data subject wants information about your Bolt journey, including details of whether/when the car was locked. She thus explicitly specifies her request (for this one trip, listing the data she wants) 

As information about the locking/unlocking of the car during the booked trip qualifies as personal data, this must be provided by means of a DSAR. 
{panel}


B. *Qualifikation as personal data:*  If we collect/process data, on when the car was locked during a ride (customer rented the car for a trip) every active locking/unlocking of the car by the user can be considered as a personal data (not included are: automated locking/ locking triggered by the system without the users interaction). This because the data is linked to the users behaviour (how did they use the car)

C. *Interest in getting the information:* does not matter because data subjects do not have to provide a reason of there request

D. *Amount of data:* Apart from the specific information on locking the car, the request is fairly general: Some of the desired information can be requested directly from the user in the app: For example, in the app under "My rides", in addition to querying ridehailing and micromobility services used, information about BoltDrive services used is also available, namely:

* Car model
* Car license plate number
* Date
* Time/address of start, intermediate stops and end
* Total duration of use
* Total kilometers

nless explicitly requested otherwise by the data subject, a request to exercise the right of access shall be understood in general terms, encompassing all personal data concerning the data subject . Limiting access to part of the information may be considered when he data subject has explicitly *limited the request to a subset.* In total, this could be seen as "information of the last trip" and the locking information could be provided in addition. 


----


*More information:*
A. *Qualification as personal data:* According to Art. 4(1), the GDPR only protects natural persons against the unauthorized processing of their personal data. The term "information" contained in the definition includes, without limitation, "any information" relating to a person, which shows that the term is to be understood broadly. This means that personal information such as identification features (name, address and date of birth), external characteristics (gender, eye color, height, weight) or internal states (opinions, motives, desires, beliefs, value judgments6) are just as important as factual information, i.e. financial and property circumstances, communication and contractual relationships as well as other relationships between the data subject and third parties and their environment.

The definition of personal data contains three components: 

* a processing component, which refers to the data, 
* a content component that relates to people and the 
* identity component, which refers to the identifiability of a person. 

With regard to the processing component, it should be mentioned that even a single piece of personal data is protected by the GDPR. The fact that the information must relate to a person and not just to several persons or an object is an independent feature of the definition, as a distinction from factual data. This criterion is separate from the identifiability of the person.

Persons do not have to be directly identifiable; instead, identifiability is sufficient. A person is identifiable if the information in itself is not sufficient to assign it to a person, but this is possible as soon as the information is linked to other information. If it is possible to identify the person using the available information and other means, such as publicly accessible sources (e.g. telephone directories, public registers, admin, etc.). All objective factors, such as the cost of identification and the time required, should be taken into account. 

With regard to the locking data, questions about the relative personal reference (the case law of the CJEU on the personal reference of IP addresses also indicates a relative understanding) can be omitted in this case, since Bolt as controller can clearly establish an absolute personal reference by comparing the different data. 

[Opinion 4/2007 on the concept of personal data|https://ec.europa.eu/justice/article-29/documentation/opinion-recommendation/files/2007/wp136_en.pdf] states that the definition includes four main building blocks. They are the following ones:

*  “any information”: From the point of view of the nature of the information, the concept of personal data includes any sort of statements about/ related to a person. It covers "objective" information, such as the presence of a certain state caused by the person: 

*The car was manually locked by the driver*

* -  “relating to”: In general terms, information can be considered to “relate” to an individual when it is about that individual. In many situations, this relationship can be easily established. For instance the data registered in one’s individual file in the personnel office are clearly “related to” the person’s situation as an employee. In some situations, the information conveyed by the data concerns objects in the first instance, and not individuals. Those objects usually belong to someone, or may be subject to particular influence by or upon individuals or may maintain some sort of physical or geographical vicinity with individuals or with other objects. It is then only indirectly that it can be considered that the information relates to those individuals or those objects.

{quote}_“A similar analysis is applicable where the data are about processes or events in the first place, for instance information on the functioning of a machine where human intervention is required. Under some circumstances, this information may also be considered as "relating" to an individual.”_ (Guidelines page 9)

*Example No. 6: car service record* _“The service register of a car held by a mechanic or garage contains the information about the car, mileage, dates of service checks, technical problems, and material condition. This information is associated in the record with a plate number and an engine number, which in turn can be linked to the owner. Where the garage establishes a connection between the vehicle and the owner, for the purpose of billing, information will "relate" to the owner or to the driver. If the connection is made with the mechanic that worked on the car with the purpose of ascertaining his productivity, this information will also "relate" to the mechanic.” (Guidelines page 10)_{quote}

The terms of this statement clearly indicate that the extent to which certain identifiers are sufficient to achieve identification is something dependent on the context of the particular situation.

Unless explicitly requested otherwise by the data subject, a request to exercise the right of access shall be understood in general terms, encompassing all personal data concerning the data subject . Limiting access to part of the information may be considered when he data subject has explicitly *limited the request to a subset.* In order to avoid providing incomplete information, the controller may consider this limitation of the data subject’s request only if it can be certain that this interpretation corresponds to the wish of the data subject. Existing duplicates needed to be removed manually. The following query logic was used to determine the rows to be deleted:

{noformat}WITH rows_to_keep AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    max(created_date) AS last_created
  FROM ng_delivery_spark.delivery_menu_vendor_menu_version_topology_item_data
  GROUP BY id
  HAVING count(*) > 1
)
SELECT
  a.id,
  a.created_date
FROM ng_delivery_spark.delivery_menu_vendor_menu_version_topology_item_data a
JOIN rows_to_keep b ON b.id = a.id AND b.last_created != a.created_date
ORDER BY id DESC;{noformat}

Rows were then deleted with the following query:

{noformat}DELETE FROM ng_delivery_spark.delivery_menu_vendor_menu_version_topology_item_data
WHERE
  (id=5348024563711807 AND created_date='2023-11-23') OR
  (id=5348024563711806 AND created_date='2023-11-23') OR
  ...
  (id=4644337115745511 AND created_date='2023-11-09');{noformat}

* {color:#0747a6}In relation to Section 8 last sentence, we don't agree with LinkedIn and generally service providers continuing processing our Personal Data even if the data has been aggregated in a manner that does not identify individuals or customers to improve LinkedIn’s systems and services. Therefore, we would like these provisions to be deleted “For clarity, LinkedIn may continue to Process Customer Personal Data that has been aggregated in a manner that does not identify individuals or customers to improve LinkedIn’s systems and services.”{color}

Please note that this is not something we can accommodate. Our position is that we will only retain data that has been both deidentified and aggregated (prior to termination), at which point is no longer considered Personal Data. We include this language here to be fully transparent. LinkedIn uses Customer Personal Data only to enable product features for which it support ongoing efforts to improve LinkedIn’s products. LinkedIn may only rely on deidentified insights from Customer Personal Data to better LinkedIn product performance. For example, we might leverage deidentified insights from customer’s ATS data to improve matching relevance in LinkedIn Recruiter, In such instances, Customer Personal Data is processed in a manner that does not identify individuals or customers to any third party.

* {color:#0747a6}In Section 9, we suggest adding that Schedule A and Schedule D shall apply as Annex B and Annex II, respectively.{color}

Can you please clarify this request?

* {color:#0747a6}Regarding Section 10, clarification is needed on whether these third-party data processors are considered sub-processors of LinkedIn.{color}

No, they are not. This was drafted for cases of integration with customer systems (which LinkedIn considers a third-party provider) e.g. LinkedIn integration with customer recruitment system.

* {color:#0747a6}In the Subscription Services Agreement, for Section 8 (Limitations of Liability), we propose that the limitation of liability should not only apply to material failure but also to any failure of LinkedIn to comply with the terms of the DPA. Additionally, LinkedIn should define the liability it seeks to avoid with the clause: “LinkedIn disclaims liability for any Personal Data Breach (as defined in the DPA), provided that….”{color}

LinkedIn disclaims Liability for any data breach where LinkedIn has no degree of culpability, negligence or misconduct. In other terms, LinkedIn will always be liable for data breach that result from any actions or omission on LinkedIn’s side.

1. Waiting for three days before deleting a driver’s account, affects our rides and driver earnings negatively: 

- for ex. 9.2% (63 in total) of newly registered Driver accounts last month (December) were copied. Hi, apologies for the delayed response. While I believe we still need input from [~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7] re product legal issues, here are my insights from privacy perspective:

* Generally, we should avoid sharing any Rider details with Drivers: 1) it might endanger the Rider, since the Driver might know where the Rider lives/works; and 2) we do have a general obligation towards our Riders to not share their personal data with the Drivers, with some small exceptions, such as lost item cases or to generally enable Drivers to provide transportation services.
* In cases that are very sensitive, such as sexual assault/attempted rape, etc. - we should not share the details with the Driver. 
* If we do absolutely need to share trip details in some cases, I would stick to the date of trip (day/month/year), without specifying the pick up/drop off time or location, as otherwise we might expose the Rider to greater risks.
* What bugs me a bit is the point raised about the Drivers not being able to defend themselves - drivers, as service providers, have a range of rules they have to adhere to, including our T&C (I leave this one for [~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7] to comment on), and even though we seek to evaluate the situation as objectively as possible, disclosing too much sensitive information doesn’t seem proportionate.
* Last thing I wanted to point out is that, according to the stats provided by [~accountid:5aab754b5c335d2a73a795f4], it seems like situations where Rider is at fault (which supposedly means that the Rider was lying) is a very small percentage if compared to situations where Driver was at fault.

Hi, [~accountid:6320602ec7601c8e4abeda47]! Apologies for the delay. We just received a response from the external counsel. They pointed out that it is likely that Bolt needs to have a postal licence as well due to taking responsibility of handling undelivered parcels (you can see the full advice below). Unfortunately, this means that we will have to postpone the launch to align with the Public Policy team. 

Here is the advice:

{quote}We have considered the below description of services of BOLT SEND in conjunction with the proposed T&Cs. We are aware of the issues on interpretation between the “provision of mere transport services” and postal services, as also confirmed at EU Level including in the [Report on Postal Definitions published by the European Regulators Group for Postal Services.|https://ecommerce-europe.eu/news-item/commission-published-evaluation-of-postal-services-directive-and-parcel-delivery-regulation/]

In Malta, the Malta Communications Authority (MCA) is the regulator for Postal Services.

We note that the local transposition of the Postal Services Directive, the Postal Services Act, (Chapter 254 of the Laws of Malta) defines a Postal Article as:

_“an article_ *_addressed in the final form_* _in which it is to be carried by a postal operator. In addition to articlesof correspondence, such articles also include books, catalogues,newspapers, periodicals and postal parcels, however so described, including packages containing merchandise with or without commercial value;”_

We also note that the way that BOLT SEND is structured includes wording in the terms and conditions that point towards “delivery” rather than “transportion”, including the fact that in the case of a failed delivery, the package can be picked up from Bolt, which would potentially be also construed that Bolt is responsible for the integrity of the postal service.

We are also assuming that when Clients order a delivery of their parcel from point A to point B, this would necessarily involve providing a final address for the parcel, which in a non-names basis call with the Regulator seems to be interpreted as a core consideration that would make the parcel a “postal article” and therefore potentially bring the service closer to a requirement of a General Authorisation.

_In Malta, Postal Services means services involving the clearance, sorting, transport and distribution of postal articles:_

_Provided that the provision of a service of transport alone shall not be considered as a postal service;_

_Clearance means the operation of collecting postal articles by a postal service provider;_

_Sorting is not defined;_

_Distribution means the process from sorting at the distribution centre to delivery of postal articles to their addressees;_

It is relevant to point out that during a call with the regulator (on a no names basis) to explore any local guidance on what would constitute “provision of a service of transport alone” and to shed more light on what they deem as “_an article_ *_addressed in the final form_*_”_, the authority just mentioned the situation of “furniture movers” which would be just transport service providers. When pressed further to comment with other examples, the authority volunteered examples of platforms such as “Bolt” (their reference!) as service providers who have/had obtained a general authorisation on the basis that they satisified the requirements of “Clearance” and “Transport” and mentioned that Bolt was previously given such an authorisation which it later terminated.

If the Bolt service would be deemed to constitute a Postal Service rather than just a “service of transport”, we are of the opinion that as the T&C’s currently stand, the Drivers are responsible for the service and therefore, would be required to individually notify the authority. Bolt could additionally be deemed to be offering a Postal Service itself if the parcels fall under the definition of Postal Articles since they would be addressed, if Bolt would hold on to them in the case of a failed delivery.

At this stage, to fully clarify whether BOLT SEND constitutes a postal service or not, or could be deemed to be a postal service or not by the Regualtor, we would need to enter into discussions with the MCA and check whether BOLT and/or the Drivers or potentially both, need to notify the regulator.{quote}

We check {{fraud-user-data}} {{/internal/user/balanceInfo}} endpoint

It calls following endpoints [in sequence|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/967a60c6a9e283da9fc091c36fe31c44a1572f21/src/platform/commerce/fraud_data/main/user_data/service/UserBalanceService.ts#L25-L26]:

* invoicing_balance {{/internal/getUserUsedCurrencies}}
* Invoicing_balance {{/internal/getBalances}}



Below is CLIENT_TIMEOUT errors returned by {{/internal/getBalances}}

{{/internal/getUserUsedCurrencies}} may return CLIENT_TIMEOUT, but much less often

[https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/r/s/Thd9C|https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/r/s/Thd9C] 

!Screenshot 2024-01-22 at 18.53.24.png|width=2547,height=1166!

*CLIENT_TIMEOUT reasons is* {{TTL exhausted before query!}}

Note: quite often TTL value is close to 0 🤔 



If we check logs for specific root_hash (e.g. 6c0a6ec7-f13e-47ae-8027-b732d464c1e7) we will see following

[https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/r/s/YraDb|https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/r/s/YraDb] 

!Screenshot 2024-01-22 at 19.04.58.png|width=2554,height=689!

*Timeouts on* {{fraud-order}} *(caller) side happens before* {{invoicing-balance}} *(callee) returns CLIENT_TIMEOUT*

Note that timeout config for {{fraud-order}} is 1750 ms and we may TTL = 1450 ms at the moment of timeout, so:

* likely, {{fraud-user-data}} {{/internal/user/balanceInfo}} call was done at the beginning of {{/internal/checkOrder}}
* {{/internal/checkOrder}} waited 300 ms for {{/internal/user/balanceInfo}} => *it’s not a problem of TTL*

Here, we also see {{ER_QUERY_INTERRUPTED}} which means that *CLIENT_TIMEOUT* error was thrown, when {{invoicing-balance}} started DB query. If we check other queries, *CLIENT_TIMEOUT* may be thrown immediately after {{/internal/getBalances}} received a query (but it will be still later than timeout happens on {{fraud-order}} side)

{color:#ff5630}*Conclusion:* {color}{{fraud-user-data}}{color:#ff5630} {color}{{/internal/user/balanceInfo}}{color:#ff5630} *spends 300+ ms on something before calling* {color}{{invoicing-balance}} {{/internal/getBalances}}
{color:#ff5630}*Either*{color}{color:#ff5630} {color}{{/internal/getUserUsedCurrencies}}{color:#ff5630} {color}{color:#ff5630}*may take 300 ms (despite 99th duration percentile is 10 ms* {color}🤔{color:#ff5630} *) or there is some slow code on*{color}{color:#ff5630} {color}{{/internal/user/balanceInfo}}{color:#ff5630} {color}{color:#ff5630}*side*{color}

I’ll try to apply some duration profiling to check what takes 300 ms.

* event loop lag

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

Hey, I’ll try to address each issue separately:

Primary issues:

# Phone masking - this needs to be fixed. I know it’s easier said and done, but we can’t create special processes just because a core functionality is not working well. Couriers and Eaters have the option to reach out to each other for a multitude of reasons, and if they are unable to do so, the issue needs to be escalated so that it can be fixed. 
# The process might be more complex than simply reporting the issue and waiting for CS to solve it, but at the end of the day, couriers need to take one photo and one screenshot and send it to CS. Our competitors in many markets already have a version of this process in place, so it’s not something unheard of. There might be a learning curve as with all new processes, but we can’t not roll out the process just because couriers might not know how to send a screenshot. 

Secondary issues: 

# , 2. and 4. At the moment it’s not clear how this could create backlog. In the four markets where this process was tested, it resulted in slightly lower average handling time and the volumes of cases have not spiked.

3. If you were following the old process, you also would have had to refund the user. Again, we haven’t seen a spike in refunds in the test markets. 

5. Might turn out to be a valid concern, but at the moment we have no way of knowing it. 

Our suggestion is to test the process and if data shows it’s not suitable for the market, you can raise another ticket and we can start the discussion again. If you have any other concerns at this time, please reach out to Roberts Mitrevics, Paul Hicks or Gunay Hajizada.

*Date:* 23 January 2024 

*Time:* 11am - 11.45am 

*Present:* [~accountid:610279859798100070592384] and [~accountid:63fe21787c30bbd6b33e09d3] 

*Discussion:* Launch of e-Scooters in Ireland update 

There is currently a hold, and this is due to the legislation requirements being approved by the minister. AD said that it is her understanding that the regulations covers e-Bikes, and addresses e-Bikes with a throttle (and this is where the current hold up is, the hold up is not to do with e-Scooters). Bolt does not have any throttle bikes in Ireland therefore this does not have any consequences for Bolt. 

+*Legislation outlines the following requirements for e-Scooters in Ireland*+ 

*Max weight - 25kg*

*Max speed - 20km*

*Max unrated power of - 500 watt*

The e-Scooter that will be launched is the Bolt 4 (The Cobra)  this is the only scooter that meets the specifications outlined in the legislation and it is reliable. The downfall is that newer models have been released that have features such as indicators and suspension and the Bolt 4 does not have this. 

Bolts sensors are on the 4, 5, 6 and a lot of the software updates apply to all scooters, this is because lots of the features are software as opposed to hardware.

The Bolt 4 was made by Bolt to order. 

They are considering renaming the Bolt 4 for Ireland, not confirmed yet. 

+*Background information on e-Scooters*+ 

*Bolt 4 (the cobra)*- [See here |https://bolt.eu/en/blog/bolt-launches-new-fourth-generation-scooter-model/] 

*Bolt 5 (the Okai)* - [See here|https://bolt.eu/en/scooters/],  this was made by a company Okai (this company manufacturers scooters for all competitor companies), loads of companies have the same scooter, Bolt has less control on modifying these, there has been a few difficulties with the Bolt 5. 

*Bolt 6 (the Cobra)* - [See here|https://bolt.eu/en/blog/introducing-bolt-6-scooter/], the 6 is cheaper than buying an Okai from another company, and the reason is because Bolt is making these, these scooters are being  made in China and being assembled in Tallinn

It would be preferred by the team in Ireland that Bolt would be launching the Bolt 6, as there is more safety features and it is the newest scooter, unfortunately due to the regulations in Ireland, Ireland can only launch the 4.  Separately to that, there is a supply chain issue, and due to Bolt winning a lot of tenders  (Milan, Brussels, and Oslo) in priority 1 cities there is an issue on supply. 

FYI - A priority 1 city is a city that is big in size, has lots of potential revenue. 

+*What are the competitors doing*+

Tier lightest scooter is 27kg, they are exploring changing the battery to get the scooters in the 25kg mark. 

Super predestrian - they are gone.

Dot - do not have an option of a lighter scooter. 

Voi - do have an option of a lighter scooter. 

Due to the regulations only 3/4 out of the 7 competitors can launch in Ireland with scooters that meet the regulations specifications. 

+*Background timeline of why there has been delays*+ 

Primary legislation signed in June 2023 - this then went to the European Commission for the tris procedure (which is when this is sent to all member states for 90 days for them to flag if there are any concerns) - The tris procedure ran from June 2023 - October 2023 the 90 days were up - European Commission come back to Ireland said they are good to go with those regulations. Then Ireland expected it to be signed as it has gone on for 4 years. Week before Christmas, [~accountid:610279859798100070592384]  spoke to the person project managing it, the issue is with the throttle and the e-Bike, they are trying to get everyone onboard. Ireland thought it would be Nov/Dec, however regulations have not been signed yet.

+*Council Bi-Laws*+ 

On the same day the minister signs the regulations, it is expected that the minister will bring in council guidelines at same time he signs the regulations. The guidelines purpose is to include bi-laws in an effort for all citifies to be the same page. 

Ireland team have not seen the guidelines yet, [~accountid:610279859798100070592384]  is hoping that Bolt would have had a positive influence on the guidelines and [~accountid:610279859798100070592384] has been having discussions regarding these. 

*Expected timeframe:* February 2024

+*Which cities will Ireland team be launching*+ 

Sligo has agreed in draft that Bolt can launch there

Carlow has signed and agreed that Bolt can launch there

Bray - They have said they are interested once scooters are legal in Ireland

Sligo template once it is finalised will be applicable for other markets, Bolt has won Port Leashe

+*Next steps*+ 

* [~accountid:610279859798100070592384] to keep legal team updated once there is movement on the guidelines and launch dates 
* Legal to ensure T&Cs are prepped for the launch - Ireland T&Cs are currently undergoing an update.

The general principle is that we have to show the lowest price of the last 30 days.

_Directive: the previous price is the_ +_lowest_+ _applied by the trader during a certain period of time, which is not less than 30 days prior to the price reduction._

W1: 2,99

W2: 1,99 (1st promo)

W3: 2,99

W4: 1,99 (2nd promo)

[~accountid:60a8d308c8c05a0069800b2a] It’s not about our developers releasing something, it’s limiting the blast radius if any of our internal system get hacked.

Any internal system can currently call any other system without any runtime checks. If an internal component gets hacked and an attacker manages to run arbitrary code, then he can potentially bring down the entire business. Can call any internal endpoint, can take any action that is exposed to internal system.

Enforcing system2system authorization at runtime would at least not allow the attacker to interact with other internal components and spread the attack. The attacker could still abuse the components that were already called by his hacked component, but at least he could not abuse all of them, thus reducing the blast radius of such a hack significantly.

As [~accountid:629715349bc7150068cdfd35] pointed out, libraries can only be tested in two ways: (1) independently in unit tests or (2) embedded in service. Option 1 works well if the library has no network interactions, nothing to mock, if it’s a collection of pure functions. Option 2 works sometimes, but what if I need to test my library independently of any client component?

There are some messy workarounds:
- dummy components, not deployed in production, only for testing purposes
- testing endpoints in components deployed to production, testing endpoints are disabled from code on live environment
- manually mocking the library dependencies in the tests → outcome is the same, but very verbose because we can’t rely on the testing framework for mock injection

All 3 options work, but they are messy in different ways. It looks to me like a missing feature of the testing framework.

PS: I understand that this is scenario is probably an outlier and there won’t be many teams (besides Geo) that would immediately benefit from it. The votes it got from the other GTLs kind of demonstrate that.

[~accountid:5bb770688eb5ad7760adbdc3] Looked at it:

As already mentioned by [~accountid:61f1059be4a724006adb49f9] this is the failure on OS level, meaning that the problem is not response’s body, but the response format itself. OS parses response data according to HTTP format specification and fails with this error when something goes wrong there. 

The problem is not related to the search experience, looking at this [report|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/TECH-85322] we can find that the same code -1017 has been received for {{getRideOptions}} , {{/mobility/search/poll}} in addition to {{getPickupData}} which has triggered the mixpanel even shown in the ticket description. 

At the same time log contains 2 {{-1001}} request time out errors located right before the error above. All of this looks suspicious and leads to the assumption that something goes wrong with the network connection. One of the possible explanations might be that if phone uses VPN and when VPN server becomes *unreachable* for some reason, the VPN might send back a response that the app isn't equipped to handle, thus resulting in the NSURLErrorCannotParseResponse (-1017) error.

[https://stackoverflow.com/a/76611906|https://stackoverflow.com/a/76611906|smart-link] 

Increase of this kind of errors on mixpanel is slowly growing and could be related to the growing amount of users in general. It appearance in March last year must be an addition of this event to the codebase.

Hi [~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7],

I had a call with David Bulafkin and the PY Ops team this afternoon and from what we discussed and the memo David shared, I understand that the “Ambassador Programme” will consist of selecting a number of drivers who will meet quarterly with the Operations team to give feedback on Bolt, make suggestions, raise concerns and issues that they and their fellow drivers are facing etc.

The selection process will be as follows: drivers who wish to be selected as “Ambassador” will have to nominate themselves via a dedicated website. The PP and Operations teams will review the nominations and shortlist a number of candidates. Ops and PP will then meet with the shortlisted drivers for 15 minutes to ensure that they will be a positive influence on other drivers.

We will then publish biographies of each candidate, explaining why they want to be Ambassadors, and ask drivers to vote for their favourite candidate.

The 20 drivers with the most votes will be appointed as Ambassadors. These 20 Ambassadors will have an annual mandate and the possibility of being re-elected for a second year. Ambassadors will receive financial compensation for the time they spend at the quarterly meetings or on Bolt's related requests.

In David’s words the reasons for establishing the so-called Ambassador Programme are as follows:

* _Serious safety concerns from drivers that has the potential to jeopardise our license_
* _Need more positive PR stories following multiple murders in PY_ 
* _Want to hear first hand from drivers what their experiences are to inform operational, policy and product decisions_ 
* _Acting to combat negative union sentiment that suggests that we don’t value or engage with drivers_
* _Drivers should represent themselves as a way to cancel out the perception that we see drivers as singular_

During our call this afternoon, David also noted that he believes the Ambassador Programme would prevent drivers from having to seek union support against Bolt, thus the programme would help reduce the risk of reclassification.

I am not sure whether, as David suggests, this programme will reduce the risk of reclassification. I am inclined to think the opposite. The way they want to construct this programme (i.e. a group of drivers who represent the interests of the rest) reminds me of trade union representations of workers in companies. In addition, these Ambassadors will be paid to perform a number of tasks at Bolt's request, such as attending meetings, completing surveys, looking into the possibility of organising their own events in their communities, and so on. This could be reminiscent of the employer-employee relationship?

Although the risk of reclassification is moderate in Paraguay for now, a law on presumption of employment for platforms is being discussed in parliament, so I think we should be very cautious. I think, if they want to move forward with this project, some adjustments/changes to the program may have to be proposed to mitigate the risks.

I look forward to your opinion on this, [~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7] . As far as I know, it is a new initiative that they want to try for the first time in Paraguay. I wonder if you have already come across this project?

For this comparison the data from the last re-training of TF-IDF version was copied to v3 bucket. Validation dataset time range adjusted so both versions were validated on last two weeks of data.

So, some natural caveats for such comparison:

* Time-based validation might be biased as evaluation only happens on short time-span. Need to repeat for different timeranges or do random split.
* To completely unbias v3 we need to split valid into valid and test. Valid is currently used to determine early stopping which is not exactly leakage, but not ideal either.
* Ideally comparisons should be done on controllable test sample (i.e. not the code splitting data, but rather split happens in one place and both version read test data in explicitly from the file).

*After the careful analysis, the following advise was provided to the team before the launch*


*The privacy team has some questions in relation to the site:*

# Link to the privacy policy at the bottom of the page leads to the Ride-hailing privacy policy. We should provide the link to the Bolt Food privacy page that should automatically define the user's location and show the [privacy policy|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/?category=delivery] for the relevant country. 
# As an alternative, we can provide a link to [the common page|https://bolt.eu/et-ee/privacy/] with all Privacy Policies where user can choose "Ordering Food"
# *Cookies:* Necessary cookies as well as marketing and analytics cookies should be aligned with food sub-page needs. We had a call on Jan 22, where [~accountid:61f1995a9e893900691a9715] confirmed that the cookies will be aligned before the launch. The visual representation and the logic will be the same as for the main [bolt.eu|http://bolt.eu/] page, but tailored to web app needs.
# The cookie banner that pops up once the page is open should include three buttons "accept", "decline all", "manage options". On call on Jan 22, we agreed with the web team and [~accountid:61f1995a9e893900691a9715] to implement three buttons to cookie banners.
# *Session cookie:* We ask for the user’s phone number, then we send an SMS code, and the user is logged-in. As this is a web page, it creates a session authentication cookie. This cookie should last only for the session (once the order is delivered to the user and some time thereafter to be able to submit a ticket to the CS) and then the user should be logged out because we cannot extend the session cookie longer than necessary for the session. This cookie is a necessary cookie, so we don't need the user's consent for this. But if we don't log out the user, this cookie requires a consent (simple "Remember me") is enough.

*Legal explanation of point 6:*

Art 5(3) of the ePrivacy Directive states that "*the storing of information,* or the gaining of access to information already stored, *in the terminal equipment of a user* is only *allowed on condition that the user concerned has given his or her consent". However, there are 2 exemptions from the user's consent, one of which is when this storage is*{{ strictly necessary to provide the service explicitly requested by the subscriber or user. }}Without the use of an authentication token/similar thing stored in a user's device, the user would have to provide a phone number and SMS code on each page request. Therefore this authentication functionality is an essential part of the service that is explicitly requested by the user. All cookies or other things that require storage of authentication information on user's device are under this rule. As Bolt can rely on the exemption described above, we should not store this authentication token/similar thing longer than for a session (make an order, deliver the order, and some time thereafter to be able to submit a ticket to the CS). It means, once the user closes a page (in case no order is made) and when the order is delivered and the user closes a page, we should log out the user from the web app. Otherwise, we need a consent as described above as we will fall outside the exemption.

*We have two options:*

* Log out the user once the user closes a page (in case no order is made) and when the order is delivered and some time thereafter (30 mins max).
* Implement "Remember me" checkbox, so it's recognized as consent to store this info longer than permitted by the exemption. However, we should have a clear purpose for storing this session cookie longer than for a session.

You can find details of this authentication tokens/cookies/etc in the relevant explanation provided by the [data protection working party|https://ec.europa.eu/justice/article-29/documentation/opinion-recommendation/files/2012/wp194_en.pdf] on this (page 6-7). They use cookies as an example, but please note, it relates to all information similar to cookies, not only cookies.

to size the issue - it looks like there are on average 1.2 sessions per user block for a 120 min timeslice interleaved test, so for every 5 users, 4 will have 1 session, and 1 will have 2 sessions. since these are likely coming from same users in similar time/place they have a higher than average probability of also being exposed to feature. so likely the dilution factor here is ~10% for session conversion metrics. metrics that sum over user-block are unaffected.

Blocked by billing team. The part of the epic on their side did not make it into Q1. See the thread [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02BZ67SKFG/p1706092894299729|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02BZ67SKFG/p1706092894299729|smart-link]

the biggest challenge i see here is that by filtering within user-block, metrics no longer match their definitions, e.g. {{Avg finished orders per user-block}} is no longer a valid label. this is fundamentally different from the kind of filtering that happens in Targeting through enrollment events, which just assign a group, but don’t filter out data within a unit, i.e. a user might only be enrolled when the are exposed to a feature, but all data is included after that point.the fix here would be to have a different scorecard. however, i would point out that the effort investment might not be totally worth it. with the user-block level filtering we would be addressing 80% of the dilution. the within user-block filtering i would size at ~2% additional (10% of remaining 20%).

Thank you for your patience, unfortunately your ticket was assigned to me even though I was OOO for some time.

Refresh grants are due when initial grant is about to be or already is fully vested. 

If employee is eligible for refresh grant and is about to be promoted at the same time then it depends on how close the fully vested date and promotion date is. If dates are close together then it makes sense to combine these grants into one bigger grant instead of doing one grant as a refresh and another one as a promotional one. However, if dates are not that close to one another (months apart) then the recommendation is to do separate grants. As always, when deciding on refresh or promotional grant size [equity compensation calculator|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BMP/pages/4178280783/Equity+Compensation+Calculator] should be used to determine the initial amount of units that could be granted, and further more taking into account total compensation and performance the final amount of units can be determined.

Refresh grants should be treated outside of comp review.

Kind regards

* The US Embassy is responsible to declare and apply for tax refund on their own. 

*Scenario 2:*

* If the US Embassy is a taxable person in SK (e.g. lease its premises to third parties which make it become a taxable person from the VAT perspective), Bolt Ops EE should issue an invoice with reverse charge VAT and using the EE VAT ID to the US Embassy.

This is a tricky question. Basically we have a question of trade-offs should we decide to use this research methodology on any issue: 

* We can select users send emails / pushes to targeted users, asking for them to give consent to research & setting up a time. This is good should we decide one-off researches per different topics, since this requires the least amount of prior setup and dependency. Has risk of a huge amount of time between ticket resolution & our followup.
* We can gather participants on an ongoing basis for all support issues (integrating to the support flow). It’s good if we need participants at almost all times on an ongoing basis for different topics. Assumes dependency on T&W (scope unknown). 
* We can be proactive, calling specific users and asking if they consent (still need it in written though). Good if we optimise for getting as many leads as possible to participate, risky because people might be creeped out if we call them out of the blue.

_Hi,_

_We do use the same logic in our automation. Example:_ [_Rider did not pay_|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CD/pages/4293427232/Rider+Did+Not+Pay]

*_Context_*_: We do believe the driver and we’re not creating any outgoing contact to the Rider just to confirm this. This is the same logic. We prefer compensation to avoid user friction._

_How are we supposed to do this if we don’t contact the Driver? Take the Rider’s word as absolute truth?_

_By prioritizing compensation in situations where direct confirmation is challenging, we aim to provide swift resolutions and maintain user satisfaction. Creating multiple outgoing contacts can indeed incur additional costs_ *_without a guaranteed resolution_*_, and our strategy focuses on pragmatic solutions to address the issue efficiently. It might not represent the "absolute truth," but trying to determine it may not always be the most efficient approach. This is particularly true considering the challenges you highlighted earlier (the Driver never replies to us, if the Driver insists the issue never happened, and the rider is lying)._ 

_I get what you're saying about checking with the Driver who denies the events, but the truth is, relying only on their side or the Rider's never will be foolproof._ 

_The compensation method not only streamlines the process for both parties but also reflects our commitment to resolving concerns swiftly._

_Let me know if you have any further questions or if there's anything else I can assist you with._

# How Szamlazz account creation works:

Currently we do not store Szamlazz account passwords on Bolt database (in szamlazz_data).

1.a.

* Hungary city team inserts account connection data to Admin-panel page [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-fiscalization/fiscalization/szamlazz/connections/list|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-fiscalization/fiscalization/szamlazz/connections/list]
* If registration is not yet done, then in code we do registration as first step in fiscalization process, but we use our Szamlazz general (not account-specific) secret, one and only general top-secret password with each request
** The data that is needed for registration:
*** loginName (from secrets - general username)
*** password (from secrets - general password)
*** agentUsername ("taxify_" + from vat code)
*** agentPassword (from secrets - agent_password (not general password))
*** agentEmail (hardcoded in conf)
*** agentName  (hardcoded in conf "Taxify Hungary Kft.")
*** company tax number, name, zip, city, address, e-mail

1.b

* Szamlazz API does not seem to have account update functionality: [https://docs.szamlazz.hu/#sending-a-receipt|https://docs.szamlazz.hu/#sending-a-receipt|smart-link] 
** Due to that fact the update process has been done manually by city team
* Update connection status functionality in Admin-panel is just to update status. It does not update the account itself.



2. 

* As it is general top-secret password, there probably is not solution to simply log in to the számlázz account and change the username
* Szamlazz has functionality which we do not use yet (but it does not help with changing VAT code and it also seems to be manual process): 
{{It is possible to use a generated Agent key for authentication instead of using a username/password in the sent XML. This means that it's no longer mandatory to use the username/password field, instead you can simply use the <szamlaagentkulcs> tag.}}
{{In order to generate an Agent key, the owner or administrator of the account needs to login to the }}[http://Szamlazz.hu|http://Szamlazz.hu|smart-link]{{  website scroll down to the bottom of the dashboard. There's a section called Számla Agent kulcsok (= Számla Agent Keys), and you can generate a key by clicking the key button on the right side. The key is generated immediately and is ready to use. You can copy it directly by clicking the icon next to it.}}

{{You can provide the key in the <szamlaagentkulcs> tag, or you can also supply the key in the and tags if you are using a webshop where you cannot use this tag (both tags should contain the same key).}}

* As a workaround I would suggest adding the same account data with different VAT code in Admin-panel page: [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-fiscalization/fiscalization/szamlazz/connections/list|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-fiscalization/fiscalization/szamlazz/connections/list]
Then our code would create a new account.

Thank you for the explanation. In a nutshell, we understand that this rider incentive should be reflected in the invoice as a discount. Here is why:

# According to the current layout the client received an invoice of € 68,90 and this is what should be booked from an accounting / tax perspective. That is the amount indicated in the expense document. However, as the client rightly points out the effective expense for the company was € 34,50.
# If I correctly understand the mechanism (looking at our PL adventures with rider incentives): (i) the incentive is granted to the rider; (ii) rider uses it so the driver does not receive the full ride price from the rider; (iii) Bolt compensates the driver for the rider incentive so that ultimately driver receives 100% of the ride price.
# This means that the amount of € 34,40 is a cost that should be allocated to Bolt and considering that the netting is not live in CZ/SK, this would have to be documented by an invoice issued by fleet to Bolt.
# Considering the above, if we reflect the rider incentive as a discount in the invoice from driver to rider, then the transactions match and each entity has its profits/expenses properly documented:
## invoice from driver to rider for € 68,90 minus discount of € 34,40 reflects effective cost of € 34,50 to rider;
## invoice from driver to Bolt for € 34,40 to support Bolt’s cost with the discount; and
## both invoices make up for 100% of the ride price received by driver.

Hey Dennis,

Sorry for the long time to reply, I have been investigating with engineering. 

Turns out there was a change on how Fleet Owner Portal reflects transactions (orders, bonuses, etc.). Before, it was when the price review or the transaction finished, but now it is when the transaction is added to the payout. 

Example 1:

Order and price review finished on 31-12-2023 at 23:50:00 on DE local time, but while the invoice was created and finalised, the transaction was added to the balance on 01-01-2024 at 00:02:00. This would mean that my Looker report will show the order on the 31st but the FOP will consider it on January 1st. 

Example 2: 

Campaign bonus finished on 31-12-2023 at 23:00:00. Despite the driver achieving the bonus, the transaction has not been added to the balance as it’s not added immediately due to some other checks that happen in the backend. Thus, the campaign bonus ends up being added on 01-01-2024 at 01:00:00, in Looker I will show it on the 31st and in FOP it will show in January 1st.

If you want to read more about it, there is this [thread|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C0576CT9MQD/p1706108126808129].

The change was done mid-December and its purpose is to reflect the actual time when the transactions are part of drivers or fleets balance, given that they will or not be included based on this. So in both examples above, the transactions wouldn’t be considered for the payout made on January 1st (imagining this was a normal workday), as there is a cutoff every Sunday at midnight on local time.

Unfortunately I can’t change this right now due to other priorities but I have it on my backlog already, so please bare with me, I should have this by the end of next week. I will make a small announcement on the commerce-germany channel when the change is complete. 

No further actions will be taken on this ticket, hence closing it.

Best,

Carlos

Dear XXX, 

We write in reference to your request we received on 19 January 2024. 

We have reviewed your request and have concluded that Bolt will not be able to fulfil your request. 

We note that you have referenced Section 60A(4)(c) of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016 which states ‘_The authorised officer requires a telecommunications operator whom the authorised officer believes is, or may be, in possession of the communications data or capable of obtaining it.’_ 

Communication Code of Practice 2018 2.18 states ‘_The term ‘communications data’ includes the ‘who’, ‘when’, ‘where’, and ‘how’ of a communication but not the content i.e. what was said or written'_

The Communication Code of Practice 2018 2.55 further defines ‘content’ as _'When one person sends a message to another what they say or what they type in the subject line or body of an email is the content. However there are many ways to communicate and the definition covers the whole range of telecommunications. What is consistent is that the content will always be the part of the communication (whether it be the speech of a phone call or the text of an email) that conveys substance or meaning. It is information which conveys that meaning that the Act defines as content.'_

Considering the above, Bolt has concluded that your request is a request for the content of communications, and as such falls outside the power of the basis you have provided. Due to this, Bolt is unable to meet its Article 6 GDPR requirements to establish a legal basis to provide the information.

In order for Bolt to adhere to Article 6 GDPR requirements, we require a reference to an adequate, specific law or regulation that authorises you to request this data. Without this, Bolt are unable to meet the requirements of Article 6 GDPR and therefore unable to assist you. 

Bolt would like to reassure you that we treat all requests from the police seriously, and we seek to assist the police wherever we are legally able to do so. If you are able to provide us with an appropriate legal basis for access to the transcripts of the call, we will further review our position concerning this matter.

Kind regards, 

Bolt

Since the EE driver in this case is a EE VAT registered, the ride invoice correctly included EE VAT 0.73€, regardless the VAT status or the place of incorporation of the rider (i.e. intermediate: the LV business client (LV VAT ID) / resale: Bolt Ops EE (LV VAT ID)). 

*Monthly invoice* from Bolt Ops EE to LV business client:

* Intermediate: Bolt Ops EE (with EE VAT ID) will charge B4B service fees and invoice under reverse charge VAT.  The document {{Pārskats LV6524-485}} is just a monthly statement summarising the business client's activities, but not an invoice.  
* Resale: Bolt Ops EE (with LV VAT ID) will charge B4B service fees and rides taken in LV with LV VAT.  For rides taken abroad displayed in the monthly invoice, no VAT will be added, i.e. shown as “Cost reimbursement for rides in EE” .

*VAT impacts* for LV business client:

* Intermediate: the EE VAT 0.73€ paid may not be credited if it doesn’t have VAT payables.
* Resale: the EE VAT 0.73€ paid is a cost and the business client cannot deduct the VAT charged as no break down the ride fee and VAT will be shown in the monthly invoice on this invoice.

Hope it helps.  Thank you.

One important thing re the legal basis for disclosing data (and I hope I can comment on it as clearly as possible - but do let me know if it’s hard to understand still):

{quote}_information disclosure can be executed in compliance with the legal grounds of vital interests as outlined in data protection law_{quote}

This is a bit problematic in accordance to recent relevant case-law, here’s why:

The recent Meta ruling has spoken on the application of this provision (i.e. on when we can base data sharing on the necessity to protect vital interests). This ruling says that “protection of vital interests” is applicable exclusively in instances of *immediate and critical threats to life or health*, thereby precluding its usage in situations that lack these acute characteristics.

So, in scenarios that do not align with the immediate and direct preservation of life or health, reliance on this legal basis for data processing is not justifiable. 

What we can base such data disclosure in this case is our legal obligation to disclose data. Usually a council (or any other authority/body) needs to refer to a specific section of a specific law that lets them request the data. If they refer it in their request - we can disclose the data.

[~accountid:5f1a9692b385da00156b98be], thanks for raising this issue. It is my understanding that in this arrangement Bolt is solely responsible for issuing payment/compensation through its platform. Therefore, we have a proper legal basis for processing the IBAN data and the customer's first/last name, as this is strictly necessary for the provision of the service. 

According to data minimisation principle, processing of personal data must be adequate, relevant, and *limited to what is necessary* in relation to the purposes for which they are processed. Personal data should be processed only if the purpose of the processing could not reasonably be fulfilled by other means. 

* Has Traficar justified why they need this personal data to confirm compensation? It seems to me that order details and a valid invoice with Traficar details are sufficient to confirm that the user involved is entitled to compensation (if they meet the agreed requirements).

In other words, we do not want to 'overshare' our customers' personal data without a clear purpose.

I think that it is mainly section 5.3 Information may be submitted after a balance of interests that is relevant to your question. We can therefore emphasize that a disclosure of requested personal data may take place with the support of Article 6.1 f of the data protection regulation. This is because we at the Police Authority have a very strong legitimate interest in processing personal data to fight crime. Even if there is no constitutional obligation to provide information or it would be incompatible with the collection purposes to disclose information to the police, disclosure should generally be permitted after a balance of interests in the individual case. All tasks that the Riksdag or the government have commissioned state authorities to perform are of public interest, as is evident from the preparatory work for the new Swedish data protection regulation. When balancing interests, it should also be taken into account that the data is normally protected by the Police Authority through the confidentiality regulations in, among other things, 18 ch. 1 and 2 and 35 ch. §§ 1 Publicity and Confidentiality Act. Against this background, a balance of interests in accordance with Article 6.1 f of the data protection regulation must generally mean that you at Bolt may disclose requested personal data, now that these are requested in the police's law enforcement activities.
