Hello [~accountid:5df755169422830caca9f633], please respond to the Police with the below:

Dear XXX,

We write in reference to your request we received on 19 January 2024.

We have reviewed your request and have concluded that Bolt will not be able to fulfil your request.

We note that you have referenced Section 60A(4)(c) of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016 which states ‘_The authorised officer requires a telecommunications operator whom the authorised officer believes is, or may be, in possession of the communications data or capable of obtaining it.’_

Communication Code of Practice 2018 2.18 states ‘_The term ‘communications data’ includes the ‘who’, ‘when’, ‘where’, and ‘how’ of a communication but not the content i.e. what was said or written'_

The Communication Code of Practice 2018 2.55 further defines ‘content’ as _'When one person sends a message to another what they say or what they type in the subject line or body of an email is the content. However there are many ways to communicate and the definition covers the whole range of telecommunications. What is consistent is that the content will always be the part of the communication (whether it be the speech of a phone call or the text of an email) that conveys substance or meaning. It is information which conveys that meaning that the Act defines as content.'_

Considering the above, Bolt has concluded that your request is a request for the content of communications, and as such falls outside the power of the basis you have provided. Due to this, Bolt is unable to meet its Article 6 GDPR requirements to establish a legal basis to provide the information.

In order for Bolt to adhere to Article 6 GDPR requirements, we require a reference to an adequate, specific law or regulation that authorises you to request this data. Without this, Bolt are unable to meet the requirements of Article 6 GDPR and therefore unable to assist you.

Bolt would like to reassure you that we treat all requests from the police seriously, and we seek to assist the police wherever we are legally able to do so. If you are able to provide us with an appropriate legal basis for access to the transcripts of the call, we will further review our position concerning this matter.

Kind regards,

Bolt

Hi [~accountid:639212cda593cb822e99192b] and [~accountid:638713f0213a315af349b00c] 

Recapping the most material points from our further discussions (and as per my comments in the [suggested comms doc|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qcimpsMEK4oPV22vtj9asM3sPg5VR1Kz0UsyPaf-MI4/edit]):

* (1) We can de-risk this campaign activity be limiting statements of confidence re: our reliability in respect of our technology - e.g. _“_+_Our technology is more reliable than ever before at matching riders with drivers_+ _- we’re so confident that we can find you an initial match that if we can’t, we’ll give you Bolt Balance credit that you can use to book a journey in the future”._ This is in-line with what Uber have done (see [here|https://www.uber.com/en-NL/blog/schedule-rides-in-advance-with-uber-reserve/]).
* (2) Consider whether any other product implemented restrictions/exclusions are needed to avoid passengers exploiting the campaign. For example, last minute cross-country rides booked for 3am, in areas where there are no supply, could be a good way of exploiting this. This is best clamped down on by limiting the ability to actually book scheduled rides where we can predict ‘no-shows’ (or keeping scheduled rides to busy routes), rather than awkwardly wording T&C exclusions.
* (3) If you can’t implement any product restrictions, to close off obvious gaps, it may be wise to reserve the right to pull the plug on the promotion - I’ve added suggested wording for you to do this. Obviously, if people DO qualify for the promotion before it is pulled, we should provide the balance. Worth keeping an eye on the campaign to see how it goes.
* (4) You need to be careful to expressly exclude circumstances where a Bolt Balance credit +*won’t*+ be provided. It’s still not 100% clear to me whether we intend to provide a voucher if a driver accepts, but then cancels. If we +*DON’T*+ want to give a voucher in these circumstances, then we ought to make that clear - because otherwise the most consumer friendly interpretation of what is written will be enforceable against Bolt.
* (5) ^^^ mostly relating to the above point - the campaign needs to make it very clear that any relevant exclusions apply, one way or another. As a rule of thumb, misleading consumers and then shunting sneaky exclusions into small print could escalate consumer complaints and even make our exclusions unenforceable, so we definitely want to avoid this. But, so long the wording as a whole looks clear and doesn’t feel sneaky, then you will have accomplished this.
* (6) As mentioned before we don’t want people saying we’re responsible for missed flights - to avoid encouraging people to make complaints / legal action, we _ideally_ should avoid saying “we’re sorry” in isolation or anything else that suggests we’re at fault (such as “we know we can’t make up for it”). By contrast, saying “we’re sorry your scheduled ride didn’t go as expected.” is OK though because it’s like saying “oh that’s too bad” rather than “oops my fault”.

In summary: if there is a commercial desire to run the campaign, then by taking into account my comments across both posts in this ticket (and in the suggested comms) you should be able to decently de-risk it 👍 

Many thanks 👋

We therefore request that you weigh up the interests and decide whether it is necessary for purposes relating to the legitimate interests of the personal data controller or a third party, unless the interests and fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject outweigh and require the protection of personal data.
In this interest assessment, it should be taken into account that the Police Authority's mission to fight crime is a constitutionally regulated and justified public interest and that it is the Police Authority's responsibility to only request data when there is a concrete need and legal prerequisites for processing by the authority. You can therefore assume that the Police Authority has a strong legitimate interest in accessing the requested information, even if the authority cannot explain the background to the request in the individual case for reasons of confidentiality. When balancing interests, it should also be taken into account that the data is normally protected by the Police Authority through the confidentiality regulations in, among other things, 18 ch. 1 and 2 and 35 ch. §§ 1 OSL.

Suggestion from PingCAP support, enable {{force-init-stats}} so that after TiDB restart, statistics are gathered before serving queries.

----

After TiDB restart, the statistics maybe not load success.
[https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/tidb-configuration-file#force-init-stats-new-in-v657-and-v710|https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/tidb-configuration-file#force-init-stats-new-in-v657-and-v710|smart-link]

h3. {{force-init-stats}} _New in v6.5.7 and v7.1.0_

* Controls whether to wait for statistics initialization to finish before providing services during TiDB startup.
* Default value: {{false}} for versions earlier than v7.2.0, {{true}} for v7.2.0 and later versions.
* When the value of {{force-init-stats}} is {{true}}, TiDB needs to wait until statistics initialization is finished before providing services upon startup. Note that if there are a large number of tables and partitions and the value of {{lite-init-stats}} is {{false}}, setting {{force-init-stats}} to {{true}} might prolong the time it takes for TiDB to start providing services.
* When the value of {{force-init-stats}} is {{false}}, TiDB can still provide services before statistics initialization is finished, but the optimizer uses pseudo statistics to make decisions, which might result in suboptimal execution plans.

Hi,

We do use the same logic in our automation. Example: [Rider did not pay|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CD/pages/4293427232/Rider+Did+Not+Pay]

*Context*: We do believe the driver and we’re not creating any outgoing contact to the Rider just to confirm this. This is the same logic. We prefer compensation to avoid user friction.

_How are we supposed to do this if we don’t contact the Driver? Take the Rider’s word as absolute truth?_

By prioritizing compensation in situations where direct confirmation is challenging, we aim to provide swift resolutions and maintain user satisfaction. Creating multiple outgoing contacts can indeed incur additional costs *without a guaranteed resolution*, and our strategy focuses on pragmatic solutions to address the issue efficiently. It might not represent the "absolute truth," but trying to determine it may not always be the most efficient approach. This is particularly true considering the challenges you highlighted earlier (the Driver never replies to us, if the Driver insists the issue never happened, and the rider is lying). 

I get what you're saying about checking with the Driver who denies the events, but the truth is, relying only on their side or the Rider's never will be foolproof. 

The compensation method not only streamlines the process for both parties but also reflects our commitment to resolving concerns swiftly.

Let me know if you have any further questions or if there's anything else I can assist you with.

Thank you. 

David

Each rider account associated with these orders was created just 5-10 minutes prior to the rides with the driver. Notably, all these accounts share British phone numbers, which aligns with a recent fraud attack involving stolen card-adding in Germany. Additionally, one of the riders has a history of chargeback issues, also suggesting the use of stolen cards. The driver's involvement in this fraudulent activity is suspected, as cashing out these stolen cards would require the driver's cooperation.

The consistent close pick-up location by the driver in each case adds another layer of suspicion regarding their potential involvement in cashing out these stolen cards. In the overall context, the driver has a total of 6 finished orders for the month of December, with count-wise half of them being fraudulent.

Considering these factors, we will maintain the current status of the driver's profile without any alterations.

I will proceed to close the ticket. Should you have any further questions or require additional assistance, please feel free to inform me by commenting on this ticket.

* the FO who wrongly received the funds should return them asap to the same account they received the money from
* they should put the 9-digit payout ID to the payment explanation
* the payout gets rejected automatically
* you change the IBAN to correct

* if the payout is not rejected automatically, Partner Payments rejects it manually

* if the mistake has been made by us, we allocate a manual compensation (however, we need to try to get the payout back first)
* if the mistake has been made by the partner, we refer to the T&C and explain that it is a partner’s responsibility to provide correct bank details (however, of course, we still can help to return the money)

Alternatively: the FO wrongly received the money can transfer the funds directly to the correct FO, if they reach an agreement.

{code:sql}select type, state, sum(total_amount) as total
from (SELECT f.id,
             f.created,
             f.city_id,
             f.user_id,
             f.order_id,
             f.total_amount,
             f.currency,
             f.payment_invoice_url,
             substr(json_extract_scalar(f.modal_json, '$.id'), 26)               AS type,
             rt.reasons,
             if(f.state = 'dept_collectors', 'sent_to_debt_collectors', f.state) AS state,
             json_extract_scalar(json_extract(f.modal_json, '$.parameters'),
                                 '$.overdue_days')                               AS overdue_days,
             from_unixtime(cast(json_extract(json_extract(f.modal_json, '$.parameters'),
                                             '$.overdue_at') AS int))            AS overdue_at,
             f.created_date
      FROM ng_carsharing.rental_car_user_behavior_fine f
               JOIN (SELECT fine_id,
                            array_join(array_sort(array_agg(t.name)), ', ') AS reasons
                     FROM ng_carsharing.rental_car_user_behavior_fine_reason r
                              JOIN ng_carsharing.rental_car_user_behavior_fine_reason_type t
                                   ON r.reason_type_id = t.id
                     GROUP BY 1) rt
                    ON f.id = rt.fine_id)
group by (type, state)
order by (state, type)sq{code}

But the. report shows gross for the 01.08-31.08 - 

!image-20240126-122711.png|width=1794,height=535!

And about the Commission invoices:

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

Hope that is make thing clear

Currently, its possible to setup buildx manually when the builder container starts. Execute the following inside the builder-0 container (beforehand, make sure that the previous buildx deployment is removed from the cluster):


{noformat}docker buildx create --name k8s --node amd64 --driver kubernetes --platform linux/amd64 '--driver-opt="namespace=builder","nodeselector=kubernetes.io/arch=amd64,bolt.eu/CostCenter=ENG-PINT,bolt.eu/Workload=BuildKit","tolerations=key=bolt.eu/Workload,value=BuildKit,effect=NoSchedule","requests.cpu=4.0","limits.cpu=4.0","requests.memory=4Gi","limits.memory=4.0Gi"'
docker buildx create --append --name k8s --node arm64 --driver kubernetes --platform linux/arm64 '--driver-opt="namespace=builder","nodeselector=kubernetes.io/arch=arm64,bolt.eu/CostCenter=ENG-PINT,bolt.eu/Workload=BuildKit","tolerations=key=bolt.eu/Workload,value=BuildKit,effect=NoSchedule","requests.cpu=4.0","limits.cpu=4.0","requests.memory=4.0Gi","limits.memory=4.0Gi"'
docker buildx inspect k8s --bootstrap
docker buildx use k8s --default{noformat}



For kubernetes setup, we need to use remote driver so builder can connect to existing remote driver on startup - [https://docs.docker.com/build/drivers/remote/#example-remote-buildkit-in-kubernetes|https://docs.docker.com/build/drivers/remote/#example-remote-buildkit-in-kubernetes|smart-link]

{noformat}select 
asc2.country_code as market,

ROUND(SUM(COALESCE( CASE WHEN cot.state in ('finished', 'client_cancelled', 'client_did_not_show')  then cot.ride_price else 0 END,0)),0) as gmv_loc,
count(distinct case when fd.invoice_issuer_reg_code != fc.reg_code and fd.invoice_issuer_vat_code != fc.vat_code then cot.driver_id end) as total_active_private_drivers,
count(distinct case when fd.invoice_issuer_reg_code != fc.reg_code and fd.invoice_issuer_vat_code != fc.vat_code and fd.invoice_issuer_is_liable_to_vat = true then cot.driver_id end) as vat_liable_private_drivers,
count(distinct case when fd.invoice_issuer_reg_code != fc.reg_code and fd.invoice_issuer_vat_code != fc.vat_code and fd.invoice_issuer_is_liable_to_vat = false then cot.driver_id end) as no_vat_liable_private_drivers,
count(distinct case when fd.invoice_issuer_reg_code = fc.reg_code and fd.invoice_issuer_vat_code = fc.vat_code then cot.driver_id end) as total_active_fleet_drivers,
count(distinct case when fd.invoice_issuer_reg_code = fc.reg_code and fd.invoice_issuer_vat_code = fc.vat_code and fc.is_liable_to_vat = true then cot.driver_id end) as vat_liable_fleet_drivers,
count(distinct case when fd.invoice_issuer_reg_code = fc.reg_code and fd.invoice_issuer_vat_code = fc.vat_code and fc.is_liable_to_vat = false then cot.driver_id end) as no_vat_liable_fleet_drivers
from ng_public.fleet_driver fd 
left join ng_public.company_order_try cot on cot.driver_id = fd.id
left join ng_public.fleet_company fc on fc.id = fd.company_id 
left join ng_public.admin_system_city asc2 on asc2.id = cot.city_id 
left join (select country, client_vat, state, classname from ng_public.invoicing_invoice_issuer group by 1,2,3,4) iii on iii.country = asc2.country_code and iii.state = 'active' and iii.classname = 'InvoiceIssuer'
where DATE(cot.price_review_finished_timestamp) >= DATE('2023-01-01') and DATE(cot.price_review_finished_timestamp) < DATE('2024-01-01')
and asc2.country_code in ( 'at', 'be', 'bg', 'hr', 'cy', 'cz', 'dk', 'ee', 'fi', 'fr', 'de', 'gr', 'hu', 'ie', 'it', 'lv', 'lt', 'lu', 'mt', 'nl', 'pl', 'pt', 'ro', 'sk', 'si', 'es', 'se')
group by 1,2{noformat}

Our goal with the procedure change of taking over the comms was to make the process more efficient for every party involved. I’m afraid that OPS handling _only_ the re-onboardings from Beehive puts us back in a disadvantaged position. 


Perhaps I would propose the following:

* OPS still reaches out to the driver via infobip
* If the driver hasn’t replied to us with missing documents in 7 days, we will double-check the initial Beehive ticket for any driver replies. If documents have been provided there, we can still proceed with the re-onboarding.

Unfortunely, this case is not suitable to leverage S3 Intelligent Tiering (S3 INT) to reduce cost, and this is due to the 14d retention policy.  S3 INT moves objects that have not been accessed for 30 consecutive days to the Infrequent Access tier and after 90 days of no access to the Archive Instant Access tier (and you can opt in to send them further to Deep Archive Access and further..) so your objects will not be there long enough to be promoted to a cheaper storage level.S3 Intelligent Tiering is generally used for longer lived objects with unknown access patterns. The S3 service tracks the access patterns and move the objects accordingly, based on the set rules.  For this there is a small management cost [2]

S3 Intelligent - Tiering * - Automatic cost savings for data with unknown or changing access patterns.
 - Monitoring and Automation, All Storage / Month (Objects > 128 KB)        $0.0025 per 1,000 objects

Which will work against you if you in this instance as you are not saving in the backend by cheaper tiering.For cheaper storage with objects with known access patterns, we have different tiering this but these are for longer lived objects (see attached slide, minimum 30 days).On the bright side -  you are already taking the absolute best approach to saving money in S3 already - which is not having the data there longer than needed !

If the retention period for this data changes, it would be worth looking into options then let me know and the s3 calculator is a good resource as well [3].  A caveat is that BOLT get special pricing negotiated in your contact, listed below.Good thinking to check options here, hope this give some insight into the complex world of s3 pricing.

{quote}Does Bolt have an obligation to refund the passenger if they complain about the trip being shorter?

*Answer: In short, no Bolt is not legally obligated to give a refund here.* Bolt provides passengers with an estimated fare, and the passenger agrees to this at the start of the journey before getting into the vehicle (contract is formed), they have consented to pay for the full journey (at the estimated rate) and therefore are not entitled to a refund if they simply exit the vehicle earlier.

Unless express agreement is provided to change the fare between the parties involved (Passenger >Driver >Bolt) this wont give rise to a refund. So for example, if there is a situation where the passenger and driver agree to cut the journey shorter, and they ensure this is changed within the App (a revised agreement on the fare), but the passenger still get charged the full fare, then we only need to refund the passenger the difference in fare amounts between the agreed fare and the revised fare (this is then reflected on what the driver gets paid).{quote}

I’ll add some more context to Andre’s message. Our initial plan (discussed in previous Privacy ticket) covered storing user data in the Looker/Presto with 2 years retention. Data stored in Looker/Presto can be easily browsed for analytical purposes. However, during the implementation we realized that we are technically limited to provide the required data retention in Looker/Presto, so we cannot proceed with storing sensitive data in there. 



As a workaround, we decided to store that data in MySQL DB (as Bolt has internal ways to delete the old data from MySQL and provide proper retention). As the access to certain MySQL DB is usually limited to an Engineering team, we decided expose the data in admin-panel, so Data Analysts/Engineering Managers/Marketing Specialists could conveniently access the data necessary for their needs (e.g. to understand if a certain  marketing email campaign is being interacted with a lot).


We will *not* expose the data in admin-panel to everyone - we want to limit the access only to the people who specifically asked for the permission via the IT Service Desk.

Side note:

I also tried to understand how CLIENT_TIMEOUT error is thrown. Note, we have TTL enabled for this service:

* InternalClientRequest use remaining TTL as timeout for outgoing requests
** Thus, {{/internal/getOrderDataById}} requests “return” client timeout (however, the service itself doesn’t return timeout responses)
** These timeout errors are caught by SequenceDataCollector try-catch
* Then there are more several data endpoint requests, which immediately return CLIENT_TIMEOUT (but are also caught by try-catch)
* The only call which is not surrounded with try-catch is call to fraud-logs-storage.
** It throws CLIENT_TIMEOUT error
** It is not logged. It is not caught
** Thus, this CLIENT_TIMEOUT is returned to CS {{support-comp-eligibility}} service.



Increasing timeout for the endpoint also increases TTL, which solve similar issues in future

*1.* You’re exactly right.

*2.* No, we’re collecting the same information. The only difference is that we’re gathering *correct* information rather than incorrect information, and that the FO provides ID for verification. We already have their ID in terms of a drivers license saved on their admin profile, the only difference here is that we are able to verify that we are typing to the correct individual.

*3.* Mostly an updating of the wording, and a bit of a fine tuning to the current process, but there is a separate ticket up for this with CS to update their KB guidelines. To explain shortly, right now, CS just forwards the ticket to Ops instead of obtaining the information from the FO, which then leads to a delayed response time in terms of that Ops then have to ask the FO about these details, rather than the details already being provided when we obtain the ticket from CS.

*4.* This is a good question. We raised this, but data security declined our request to have the same process as Germany, which is interesting indeed. Ticket for this has been closed, but please see the below information from the ticket:

_”Hi!_

_While this might make the process smoother for Ops, this presents a serious security risk to the banking information and other sensitive and private data collected by such third-party tools/forms used._

_These forms might not offer the same level of security as Beehive, especially when they are not designed specifically to collect and handle sensitive financial data. Although I have seen that for example, typeform has met some compliance requirements, going this route simply adds to the high-impact risks that could occur when these tools are exposed to security breaches. The risks far outweigh the business benefits outlined._

_Additionally, by collecting bank details through an online form, there is an increased risk of phishing attacks. Fraudsters could create fake forms to mimic the legitimate process, tricking customers into submitting their financial details._

_I suggest looking into ways to enhance the existing process while maintaining all interactions and data exchanges within Beehive or Bolt’s internal tools, under our control, and where the security team can also monitor and support security-related concerns.”_

* _“If the agent calls D after receiving written confirmation to share the phone number, they just say that number to D” →_ To call the driver agents are using the phone number registered on the driver’s profile, thus additional verification isn’t needed.

Even if the driver agreed to share the phone number on a phone call - after the call the message must be sent to obtain written consent. 
* Templates in local languages - unfortunately we can’t provide translations in every language as it wouldn’t be possible to document them all in the article. Since agents know their local language, they need to adapt the template to their languages by themselves.

*TL; DR*: *I advise not to accept the request from Allianz for us to contract users directly and waive liability of Allianz for their users' activity as Ride Booker is designed to be a b2b offering.*

[~accountid:635ba1b276b91b62562e3686] [~accountid:60b2030ffe01e80069c64f5f] _for internal purposes_ please find my summary from the legal/regulatory end below - (a) how should we be providing RB, (b) how are we currently providing it, (c) what would entertaining Allianz' request mean to all this. Happy to support the direction of travel as you see fit.

*(A) How should we be providing Ride Booker?*

*vs*

{color:#ff5630}*(B) How we are currently providing Ride Booker?*{color}

* Agreement for the use of Bolt platform is between Bolt and a Business Customer (/) 
* Agreement for the use of transportation services is between a fleet/driver and a Business Customer (!)  

Not directly engaging with the end users will enable us to (i) steer clear from the application of consumer regulations (which have not been analyzed at all for this product), e.g. starting with rider age and identity verification up to our obligations related to rider suspension from the platform, and (ii) ensure we comply with certain obligations to provide pre-trip information to the client (see e.g. [for PL|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1xjttm8l2ccznZM69lGeCcErfCYqouHbToKftRe-ceAY/edit#gid=0]) who in such case we would consider to be the Business customer. 

{color:#ff5630}Currently we’re sharing with a user the regular rider T&C’s which are not only off the point in many instances (see {color}[{color:#ff5630}here{color}|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-dBLG58NqhdORtFd7SKRC9OXjJFAadvRXsWJIMTJFsg/edit]{color:#ff5630} the redline and comments following an initial reading), are not enforceable towards consumers nor compliant with b2c regulations, it is also not aligned with the whole b2b idea of the product (via-a-vis the UI, billing and payments setup).{color}

* Users remain in the role of third party beneficiaries with whom we’d share a mere code of conduct type of document via SMS (URL) for informational purposes (requiring no acceptance) (!) {color:#ff5630}As said above - currently we send the regular rider T&C’s which is confusing at best.{color}
* Liability for any cost/damage caused by users remains with Allianz. (/) That is one the key reasons (next to the limited scale of Ride Booker use to begin with) why we have been somewhat relaxed so far despite the above issues.
* Acknowledged internal decision on the safety features (equally for drivers and for the riders) which are not (entirely) available due to Bolt rider app not being in play (!) {color:#ff5630}Product has now been pulled in but we are still scratching the surface as for understanding the gap and taking any steps to closing/ accepting it.{color}



*(C) Allianz is principally requesting us to move to the opposite direction from (B).*

As not only (i) we’d be losing a contractual safeguard against possible damages, but perhaps even more importantly (ii) we’d be making it a b2c offering which it is not intended to be and for which we don’t have compliance and safety solutions (nor quite possibly even all the relevant questions yet) . The privacy perspective has not been looked at as well. The T&C enforcement really is just another matter among others in that respect.

And all this pot needs to be looked also considering the b2b2b2…2c angle, and again not only from the T&C enforcement and liability perspective but the overall compliance and safety.

Should the decision be to nevertheless pursue contracting users directly for Ride Booker rides and waiving Allianz' liability in that regard then this matter should be prioritized for MVRA. The changes needed for this are of “enterprise level”, and cannot continue to be catered from the BAU resources Legal has for supporting negotiations (it other words it has sucked and will continue to suck up too much time in the sake of other deals). Until then Legal focus will rather go on closing the gap between (A) and (B) above for the majority of our Business customers.

Best,

A.
